items.title: Rational root certificate
items.note: The closed box is {x : ‖x - r̄‖∞ ≤ 10^-30} (Vec 2 carries the sup norm), a root is a zero of P. "(art:seed_rho) holds" is read as: the explicit ρ = 129(c-8d)/((16c-127d-16)(127c+16d+129)) of failure.tex:80-83 satisfies 0.060 < ρ < 0.061 at every point of the box (the definition part of art:seed_rho is the failure.tex agent's item). Proved from the library: contraction of the Newton map N(h) = h - M P(r̄+h) on the box (exists_unique_root) and the coarse bounds 318/1000 < c < 319/1000, -1026/1000 < d < -1025/1000.

root_certificate is proved along this proof (library exists_unique_root: the Newton map is a contraction of the closed box, its fixed points are the roots). Undisplayed steps stated in Lean: the index set has eighteen monomials (certIndex_card); D = DP(r̄) is the library J and adj(D)/det D the library M (jacobian_eq, adjugate_inverse_eq); a_{i,ν} is the library coefficient of the monomial (certCoeff_word, via the Taylor lemma partialIter_of_expansion for iterated partial derivatives); |h^ν-k^ν| ≤ |ν| r ‖h-k‖ and the Lipschitz bound 7000r (newton_lipschitz); contraction and root (newton_contracting, fixed_iff_root); the root box lies in 318/1000<c<319/1000, -1026/1000<d<-1025/1000 (root_box_coarse); multiplying endpoints gives 60/1000 < ρ < 61/1000 (coarse_ratio). "compare Rump [Theorem 13.3]": a literature comparison only; the Lean proof does not use it (the contraction argument is proved directly).

Stated with D (hD: D i j = ∂P_i/∂x_j(r̄), the entries of fderiv ℝ P r̄), A = (det D)⁻¹ • adj D and a_{i,ν} as variables with their defining equations (display 005, with ∂^ν = partialIter, iterated one-variable derivatives ∂₁^{ν₁}∂₂^{ν₂}). The maxima over i are bounded for every i; |ν| = ν₁+ν₂; the index set {2 ≤ |ν| ≤ 5} is certIndex.

certCoeff A i ν is literally -(1/(ν₁!ν₂!)) Σ_j A_ij ∂^ν P_j(r̄) with ∂^ν = partialIter ν (iterated derivatives, ∂₁^{ν₁}∂₂^{ν₂}). certCoeff_word identifies a_{i,ν} with the library coefficient of the monomial for the eighteen ν with 2 ≤ |ν| ≤ 5 (Taylor coefficients of polynomials, partialIter_of_expansion).
N is a variable with N h = h - A P(r̄+h); the conclusion includes AD = I ("its linear part vanishes because AD = I").
Stated with the Lipschitz bound of the same sentence: ‖N h - N k‖∞ ≤ 7000 r ‖h-k‖∞ on the r-ball, and ‖N h‖∞ ≤ 10^-50 + 7000 r² < r, r = 10^-30.
Stated at every point of the closed box (which lies in the coarse box of lines 83-84).

This proof, with the interval certificate of lines 141-200, proves the corrected Lemma art:seed_cycle (BfgsCoverage.Article.Failure.seed_cycle: the query list is Table art:trial_table for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0). The printed lemma omits the range of (c₁,c₂) and is a DISCREPANCY item of the failure register (M11); the certificate uses the Armijo constant 1/3 in its acceptance quantity (display 015). "the algebraic part of Lemma art:seed_cycle" (failure.tex:100-120); the other part is the interval certificate of the subsection "Sound enclosure of every query" (lines 141-200, outside any proof environment, covered by its own items). Undisplayed steps stated in Lean: B(H,g,g⁺,α) = inverseBFGS H (-αHg) (g⁺-g) (update_def); the first update (SeedCycle.first_update); the middle update is C+βE (SeedCycle.middle_update gives the explicit middleMatrix); at a root β = 1/4 and γ = 1/16 (beta_gamma_root); s₀+s₁+s₂ = -(1-ρ)z₀ (displacement_closure); the matrix closure at the root (SeedCycle.source_cycle); positive curvature (g_{j+1}-g_j)ᵀs_j > 0 and positive definiteness (source_accepted_certificate, source_metric_posDef). Wording point, not an error: lines 120-123 call the two projection factors "the orthogonal projector onto (g₀-g₂)^⊥" and say "their sum" is ρ̃I; precisely, the sandwiched term (I-P)M₂(I-P) equals ρ̃(I-P) and the rank-one term equals ρ̃P, P the projector onto span(g₀-g₂).
β, γ, ρ̃ are the library SeedCycle.beta, gamma, rhoTilde (rfl).

For arbitrary (c,d) with U, V, R, K, T, Y, U+129 > 0 ("the positive factors above"); β, γ, ρ̃ are variables with the defining equations of display 009; M₁, g₀, g₁, g₂ are written out; B is SeedCycle.update (update_def).
At a point with the positive factors where P = 0 ("Equations (art:seed_polynomials) give exactly β=1/4 and γ=1/16", beta_gamma_root), with ρ the explicit formula of art:seed_rho.

The display defines the interval operations; together with line 157 ([a,b]⁻¹ = [1/b,1/a] when 0 ∉ [a,b]) and lines 151 and 158 ("encloses", "These inclusion rules follow from order on the reals") the claim is that each rule is an inclusion rule. interval_rules states the four rules as enclosures (Bounds a x b is x ∈ [a,b]).
Stated as: the root box lies in the first two intervals; on them the denominator of ρ is positive and ρ ∈ [6019,6021]/10^5 (prose/005); the root and its ρ lie in the query box.

"use p₀ = …": the directions p_j = -M_j g_j of Lemma art:seed_cycle at the root (M₀ = I, M₁, M₂ of art:seed_matrices, SeedOrbit.metric) are the displayed vectors, and they are the library SeedOrbit.direction used by the certificate.

With lines 186-187. query_lower_bounds: at the root every expression of row q exceeds queryLowerBound q = (1/10^4)·(729, 2417, 145, 75, 5964, 2682, 1041, 221, 20)_q. query_lower_bounds_box proves the bounds at every point of the query box art:query_box, by the interval rules (generated chains rawRow0 … rawRow8, each endpoint checked by norm_num). items.anchor: The remaining task is finite because one cycle has only nine queries.
items.note: The nine queries of one cycle: for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0 (the parameter range of the theorems) the three searches from (z_j,M_j) make the 1+3+5 = 9 trials of Table art:trial_table (A/failure/prose/022, Failure.seed_search), the nine listed queries of art:seed_query_bounds (A/failure/disp/009). As in A/failure/prose/002, the sentence is read for the parameter range used in the article; without a range the phase-2 query list is longer for c₁ > 0.37521 (the discrepancy of Lemma art:seed_cycle and Table art:trial_table, M11).

items.anchor: A positive derivative at each accepted query supplies weak Wolfe for every permitted curvature constant.
items.note: At each accepted row, ∇G(q)ᵀp_j > 0 and the weak Wolfe test of art:failure_tests holds for every c₂ > 0 (in particular every permitted c₂ ∈ (c₁,1)).

items.anchor: Strict value increase at each rejected query makes Armijo fail, so the routine reaches exactly the next displayed bisection.
items.note: At each rejected row G(q) > G(z_j), the (non-strict) Armijo test fails for every c₁ > 0, and the specified search records the length and continues with upper bracket α and the bisection (α_lo+α)/2.

items.anchor: For the three base points, the designated active gaps are positive as well.
items.note: Positive active gaps, 3 ± g_kᵀx > 0 for every k, 2 - x₂ > 0 and positive designated active value at the three base points and the nine queries; and art:seed_query_bounds (|g_iᵀz| < 3, [z]₂ < 2, G(z) > 0). The positivity comes from the library's interval certificate on the query box (AlgebraicSeedOracleData); the bounds are not displayed in the paper.

items.anchor: The strict active gaps also give differentiability on a neighborhood of each query.
items.note: Near each query G is differentiable with gradient g_i (strict activity is an open condition).

items.anchor: Together with the matrix identities, these calculations complete the proof of Lemma~\ref{art:seed_cycle}.
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 with M11: the lemma now states the range 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3, c₂ > 0, and these calculations prove it (Lean: Failure.seed_cycle): the acceptance quantity of line 181 is the Armijo test with c₁ = 1/3, so it holds for every c₁ ≤ 1/3; the positive slope gives weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0 (positive_slope_wolfe); a rejected query fails Armijo for every c₁ > 0 (increase_rejects_armijo). seed_cycle_range_counterexample shows that the range is needed.

The strict inequalities (the margins art:seed_margins, A/failure/disp/008; the value increase at every rejection, A/failure/prose/020; Armijo for c₁ ≤ 1/3 and weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0 at every acceptance, A/failure/prose/021) force the specified search to choose that cycle for the parameter range of the theorems (A/failure/prose/022). These are the parts of Lemma art:seed_cycle that hold as printed, as in A/failure/prose/002 for the parallel sentence of failure.tex:15; the range-free query-list claim of the lemma is its discrepancy (M11).

resolved_discrepancies.description: "Together with the matrix identities, these calculations complete the proof of Lemma art:seed_cycle" (seed_certificate.tex:199-200) asserts the lemma as printed. The printed lemma fixes no line-search constants, and its query-list claim is false for every c₁ > r₂, 0.37520 < r₂ < 0.37521 (discrepancy of A/failure/lemma/art:seed_cycle, M11; Lean: Failure.seed_cycle_range_counterexample, c₁ = 0.38, c₂ = 1/2). The calculations of this appendix prove the corrected lemma, for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0 (Lean: Failure.seed_cycle): the acceptance quantity g_jᵀz_j + αg_jᵀp_j/3 - g_iᵀq > 0 of line 181 is the Armijo test with c₁ = 1/3, hence holds for every c₁ ≤ 1/3; the positive quantity αg_iᵀp_j gives weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0 (positive_slope_wolfe); a rejected query fails Armijo for every c₁ > 0 (increase_rejects_armijo). Same issue as the lemma; no separate correction is needed once the lemma states the range.
